q: How does biomass co-firing change a coal power plant's reported emissions?
title: Biomass co-firing at a coal plant
short: CO2 from the biomass pellets is biogenic, so it is reported separately and not added to the plant's Scope 1. Methane and nitrous oxide from burning them still count. Fossil CO2 falls with the coal it replaces. The Ministry of Power's policy asks coal plants to co-fire biomass pellets.
audience: Power plant operators and captive power users

ul: Scope 1 fossil CO2: coal burned, from tonnes and lab GCV.
Biogenic CO2: pellets burned, as a separate line.
Methane and nitrous oxide from both fuels, in Scope 1.
Upstream pellet processing and transport: Scope 3 Category 3.

p: Grid consumers use the CEA grid factor, which reflects the mix over time. A captive user can use the plant's own factor if it buys directly from that plant.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
